title: PPF publishes 20th edition of The Purple Book
note: Establishes the size and shape of the PPF-eligible UK DB universe. Figures describe the position at 31 March 2025: 4,840 eligible schemes (down from 4,974), 8.6 million members, about 0.7 million active members, 71% of assets in bonds and bond proxies, s179 net surplus of £214bn, funding ratio 125%. Total assets are not stated on the press release page. The s179 basis values PPF-level compensation, not full buyout cost.

title: What TPR does and who we are
note: Establishes TPR's own description: 'the public body that protects workplace pensions in the UK'. The page does not list the statutory objectives; those are in section 5 of the Pensions Act 2004.

title: The Investment Consultancy and Fiduciary Management Market Investigation Order 2019
note: The CMA Order that introduced mandatory competitive tendering for fiduciary management and objective-setting for investment consultants. Known here from search results and law-firm summaries; the Order text itself was not read. The trustee-side duties were later moved into pensions regulations overseen by TPR (see W1-S04).

title: Tender for fiduciary management services (detailed guidance)
note: Establishes the tender threshold ('20% or more of the manageable assets are managed by one or more FMPs'), the qualifying tender process ('bids from at least three unconnected FMPs'), effective 1 October 2022, and TPR's description of fiduciary management as 'a governance model through which trustees delegate' (definition truncated in the text retrieved). Last updated August 2022.

title: Financial stability buy/sell tools: a gilt market case study
note: The Bank's own account of the September–October 2022 LDI episode. Establishes the mechanism (falling net asset values, deleveraging by selling gilts, 'an adverse feedback loop took hold') and the scale: £19.3bn of gilts bought between 28 September and 14 October 2022 (£12.1bn conventional, £7.2bn index-linked). Only the first part of a long page was read.

title: Regulation (EU) 2017/1131 on money market funds, Chapter IV, Article 33 (as retained in UK law)
note: Establishes the LVNAV rule: where the constant NAV per unit deviates from the market-based NAV 'by more than 20 basis points', the following redemption or subscription is at the market-based NAV. This is the retained UK text; it does not show any later FCA rule changes.

title: Automatic enrolment detailed guidance 4: Pension schemes under the employer duties, Appendix C
note: Source for the automatic enrolment minimums on a qualifying-earnings basis: 8% total, at least 3% from the employer, in force since April 2019. Known from the search result summary of the TPR page; page not read in full. Other pensionable-pay bases have different minimums.

title: Local Government Pension Scheme (England and Wales): Fit for the Future – technical consultation: summary of responses and government response
publisher: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (GOV.UK)
note: Source for the structure of the LGPS in England and Wales: 86 administering authorities, eight asset pools since 2015, consolidating to six under the Fit for the Future reforms. Known from search results quoting government and adviser summaries; page not read. Final commencement status and pool membership are covered by the UK institutional research stream, not here.

title: UK money market reform
note: Industry explainer cited only for the statement that the UK regime keeps three MMF structures (public debt CNAV, LVNAV, VNAV). Known from a search snippet; a manager's commentary, not a primary source. The primary definition is in Regulation 2017/1131 (W1-S06).
